environment.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti; AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D; Linux

protocol.blockOrder: wall/profile, then profile/wall, alternating by block
protocol.wall: unprofiled awaited request milliseconds; loading, tuning and fixture hashing excluded
protocol.gpu: separate instrumented per-kernel GPU timestamps; profiling changes dispatch passes and may change optional paths; not application latency
protocol.kernelShare: per-label median divided by the sum of label medians; not a share of wall latency
protocol.description: Eleven Q8 models, three deterministic request lengths, nine samples after three warmups, two wall/profile blocks per runtime. Sequential catalog captures and a separate resident paired control are retained independently.

improvements.name: Clef whole-request latency
improvements.scope: Clef Flash Q8 · Chromium · medium text request
improvements.reason: Sequential full-catalog medians improved at all three lengths. The paired CPU-only finish replay isolates the head change. It does not measure a whole-request speedup. Recorded Clef public noul outputs matched. Native logits are not exported.

improvements.name: Qwen final-block row pruning
improvements.scope: Kev 0.8B Q8 · Chromium · loaded-weight final block, 161 source rows to 3 selected rows
improvements.reason: Complete selected-row intermediates and gathered scorer outputs match bit for bit. Timings cover the final gather/RMS/gate-up/SiLU/down operation, not the whole model. Whole-model results remain mixed.

improvements.name: Gemma long-context attention
improvements.scope: Chromium · H256, 8 query heads, 1 KV head, window 512, 602 tokens · isolated registered kernels
improvements.reason: Full outputs, CPU reference checks and sentinel guards passed before and after timing. Selection requires stable gains at 257, 512 and 602 rows for the exact dimension/window family. Attention calibration increased from 82.7–90.9 ms to 499.7–612.3 ms within the unchanged 750 ms deadline. No whole-model or camera speedup is claimed.

improvements.name: Matched-tuning resident controls
improvements.scope: Laya and Kev 0.8B Q8 · Chromium · serialized calibration, then resident ABBA/BAAB pairs
improvements.reason: Median paired changes: The median paired changes for laya are +0.85% / +0.42% / 0.00%. The median paired changes for kev-0.8b are -0.83% / +1.46% / -0.36%. These controls narrow the earlier regression finding without replacing the original sequential measurements.

improvements.name: Full catalog results remain mixed
improvements.scope: All eleven available Q8 models · three request lengths
improvements.reason: Every case remains visible below. Laya and Kev 0.8B have slower sequential wall medians. The available evidence does not conclusively attribute them to noise.

improvements.name: Submission fence candidate
improvements.scope: Independent synthetic chunk-completion experiment · Chromium and Firefox
improvements.reason: The output guard passed, but the candidate did not establish a robust timing benefit. Exact experiment source and raw results are archived. Its runtime code was reverted.

limitations: Results apply to the recorded hardware, browser, pack hashes, runtime bytes and fixtures. They do not establish universally fastest kernels or model accuracy.

The initial full catalog baseline and candidate were separate sequential campaigns. Host load changed. Mixed wall results, including Laya/Kev 0.8B slowdowns, remain slower observations without a conclusive noise attribution. The resident paired control is archived separately.
GPU profiles are separate instrumented requests and change execution. GPU-time changes cannot be subtracted from wall latency or promoted to an application speedup.

The whole-request table contains only eleven available Q8 models in Chromium, three deterministic text-request shapes, and two blocks per runtime. It does not establish BF16 catalog, worker/UI, batch, mobile, camera sensor-to-screen performance or FPS.

Raw distributions matched for 9 models, and recorded public outputs matched for Laya/Clef. Each reported comparison difference was 0 at the unchanged declared tolerance 0.0005. Laya/Clef do not export native logits/raw distributions. Rounded-output equality does not establish logit equality. Numerical agreement is not an accuracy benchmark.
Qwen final-block and Gemma attention improvements are scoped kernel/composite measurements. Their full-model request medians remain mixed. No whole-Qwen or whole-Gemma speedup is claimed.

Earlier v1 Qwen Q8 guards are retained as historical numerical evidence. Final claims use the new candidate-v2 Q8 and BF16 guards. Failed poison/plumbing and preliminary captures do not contribute passing cases.

Some Qwen cache-extension fixtures did not produce a reusable native-tokenizer extension. Exact responses passed, but extension-path coverage is not established where the raw guard names this limitation.

The Clef CPU replay times only synchronous kevala_clef_finish on identical captured inputs. GPU backbone, prepare, input copies, hashes, loading and compilation are excluded. Raw logits are not exposed. Exactness covers serialized public responses.

No model weights, coordinator sub-pack, hidden input arrays or lexical input arrays are included in the archive. Only their hashes/byte counts, source identities, fixture responses and raw timing/output checks are retained.
The rejected completion-fence implementation is preserved as a source snapshot and raw experiment only. Its runtime change is absent from the final candidate.

The initial resident-control attempt overlapped both engines' GPU calibration. Kev selected different recurrence kernels between arms, so those timings do not isolate the code change. Original captures and exact harness sources are archived as excluded control evidence. Corrected controls must serialize calibration and record load order.
